rule: No sentence in this file describes a program in its own words. Every claim is a verbatim quote from a cached authoritative document (data/sources/), located by exact match at load time. A quote that cannot be found is dropped and reported, never shown. Program names and the needs they map to are this system's labels, not claims about the program.

programs.name: FEMA Housing Assistance (Individuals and Households Program)
programs.gate_note: Available only where the declaration includes Individual Assistance for your county.

claims.quote: Funds for temporary housing while you are unable to live in your home, such as rental assistance or reimbursement for hotel costs
Funds to support the repair or replacement of owner-occupied homes that serve as the household's primary residence
IHP assistance is not a substitute for insurance and cannot compensate for all losses caused by a disaster.
For certain types of assistance, FEMA must confirm the disaster-damaged home is your primary residence.

If you have insurance coverage, you will need to give FEMA proof of the insurance settlement or a letter explaining you were denied coverage before FEMA can determine what assistance you are eligible for.
you can complete an application for FEMA Individuals and Households Program assistance at DisasterAssistance.gov.
You can also apply in person, online, or by phone.
The standard FEMA registration period is 60 days following the date that the President declares an incident a major disaster or an emergency.

programs.name: FEMA Other Needs Assistance (Individuals and Households Program)
programs.gate_note: Available only where the declaration includes Individual Assistance for your county.

claims.quote: Funds for other uninsured or under-insured disaster-caused expenses and serious needs

Disaster assistance may include money for temporary housing needs, repairs to owner-occupied homes, personal property loss, medical expenses, funeral expenses, and other serious disaster-related needs or expenses not covered by insurance or other means.
Medical and dental. Necessary expenses to assist applicants with medical and dental costs
Funeral. Necessary expenses to assist applicants with funeral costs
Child care. Necessary expenses to assist applicants with child care costs
Personal property. Necessary expenses to assist applicants whose primary residences were damaged by the disaster with personal property costs
you can complete an application for FEMA Individuals and Households Program assistance at DisasterAssistance.gov.
You can also apply in person, online, or by phone.

programs.name: Disaster Unemployment Assistance
programs.agency: U.S. Department of Labor, through your state workforce agency
programs.gate_note: Tied to a presidentially declared major disaster and run by the state workforce agency. Whether it was approved for your area is not in FEMA's declaration data, so confirm with the state.

claims.quote: If you couldn't work as a direct result of a presidentially declared major disaster, you may be eligible for Disaster Unemployment Assistance (DUA).
Became unemployed, including self-employed individuals, as a direct result of the presidentially declared disaster;
Not qualify for regular unemployment insurance benefits from any state;
Establish that the work or self-employment they can no longer perform was their primary source of income.
Be a U.S. citizen, non-citizen national or a qualified alien;
These services are the responsibility of the U.S. Department of Labor, funded by FEMA, and administered by the affected state, tribal, or territorial workforce agency.

programs.name: Crisis counseling and the Disaster Distress Helpline
programs.gate_note: The Disaster Distress Helpline runs year-round. Local crisis counseling teams depend on the declaration.

claims.quote: For free and confidential crisis support in any language, call or text the Disaster Distress Helpline at 800-985-5990.

This toll-free, multilingual, crisis support service is available 24/7 to all residents in the U.S. and its territories who are experiencing emotional distress related to natural or human-caused disasters.
free and confidential crisis counseling and mental health support may be offered in your area.

All individuals, regardless of citizenship and immigration status, affected by a major disaster may be eligible for crisis counseling assistance, disaster legal services, disaster case management, disaster supplemental nutrition assistance program and other non-monetary, in-kind emergency disaster-relief programs.

programs.name: Disaster Legal Services
programs.agency: FEMA with the American Bar Association Young Lawyers Division
programs.gate_note: Tied to a presidentially declared major disaster; whether it was activated for your area is not in FEMA's declaration data.

claims.quote: Disaster Legal Services (DLS) provides legal help to survivors affected by a presidentially declared major disaster.
These services are available to survivors who qualify as low-income and are limited to cases that would not normally incur legal fees.
New wills, powers of attorney and other legal papers lost in the disaster
Home repair contracts and disputes with contractors and/or landlords
DLS attorneys are not FEMA employees.
They do not share information with FEMA.

All individuals, regardless of citizenship and immigration status, affected by a major disaster may be eligible for crisis counseling assistance, disaster legal services, disaster case management, disaster supplemental nutrition assistance program and other non-monetary, in-kind emergency disaster-relief programs.

programs.name: Disaster Case Management
programs.gate_note: Available only if approved for the declaration; FEMA's Helpline can say whether it was.

claims.quote: You may be eligible to get a case manager to help with your recovery-if approved for the presidentially declared major disaster.
Call FEMA's Helpline at 1-800-621-3362 to see if case managers are available in your area.

programs.name: SBA disaster loans
programs.gate_note: SBA lends after declared disasters. Whether SBA loans were offered for your specific declaration is announced by SBA and is not in FEMA's declaration data.

claims.quote: low-interest disaster loans designed to help businesses of all sizes, homeowners, renters, and private nonprofit organizations recover from declared disasters.
If you disagree with FEMA's decision, you may appeal within 60 days of the date of the letter.
Applicants must file their appeal within 60 days after the date that we notify the applicant of the award or denial of assistance.
When submitting any documentation or information to FEMA, you must include your FEMA application number and disaster number on every page.
You can submit your appeal documents online, in person, by mail or by fax.
If you have questions regarding your letter or how to file an appeal, call the FEMA Helpline at 1-800-621-3362.

status_notes.quote: The parent or legal guardian of a minor child who is a U.S. citizen or qualified alien applies for assistance on behalf of the minor child, so long as they live in the same household.
Individuals should consult an immigration expert to verify if they meet the immigration status requirements for FEMA disaster assistance.
Additionally, voluntary agencies provide help regardless of citizenship or immigration status.

fraud_warnings.quote: DHS, FEMA, SBA, and other federal agencies will never charge applicants for disaster assistance or help in filling out applications.
Never ask for your nine-digit registration number. They already have it in their records.
Not ask for bank information. FEMA never charges a fee for an inspection.
Always wear an official government badge to identify themselves. Ask the person to show you their identification.
Don't pay more than half the costs of repairs in advance.
If you receive a letter from FEMA but did not apply for assistance, please call our Helpline at 800-621-3362 between 7 a.m. to 11 p.m. ET daily.

late_registration.quote: After the standard or extended registration period ends, FEMA will accept late registrations for an additional 60 days.

late_registration_reason.quote: We will process late registrations for those registrants who explain the reason for the delay in their registration.

extension.quote: FEMA may extend the registration period when the State requests more time to collect registrations from the affected population.

language_need.quote: Let FEMA know if you or anyone in your household has a disability or language need.

not_all_losses.quote: FEMA's Individual Assistance programs are intended to meet only essential needs and are not intended to cover all losses.

no_duplication.quote: However, you cannot receive assistance for the same exact need from more than one program or entity, including your insurance.

distress_line.quote: call or text the Disaster Distress Helpline at 800-985-5990.

fema_helpline.quote: call our Helpline at 800-621-3362 between 7 a.m. to 11 p.m. ET daily.

immigration_expert.label: An immigration expert
immigration_expert.quote: Individuals should consult an immigration expert to verify if they meet the immigration status requirements for FEMA disaster assistance.

legal_aid.label: Disaster Legal Services
legal_aid.quote: Disaster Legal Services (DLS) provides legal help to survivors affected by a presidentially declared major disaster.

identity_theft.label: IdentityTheft.gov
identity_theft.quote: Visit IdentityTheft.gov for more information and steps you can take if you suspect you're the victim of identity theft.
